subject: Accounting
title: Closing the Books
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Closing the Books.

hook.text: At year end, accountants perform a ritual: closing the books. Temporary accounts go to zero.

buildup.text: Revenue, expense, and dividend accounts are temporary—they reset each period.

discovery.text: Their balances transfer to retained earnings, a permanent account that carries forward.

twist.text: Skip closing entries and next year's income statement includes last year's numbers too.

climax.text: After closing, only assets, liabilities, and equity carry balances into the new year.

punchline.text: Close the old chapter before starting a new one.

quiz.question: What happens to revenue accounts at year end?

details.summary: Closing the books is the process of finalizing all accounts at the end of an accounting period. Revenue and expense accounts are zeroed out and transferred to retained earnings, preparing the system for a fresh start in the new period.
details.whyItMatters: Without closing entries, revenue and expenses would accumulate indefinitely, making it impossible to measure performance for individual periods. Closing isolates each period's results.
takeaways: Closing entries zero out all revenue, expense, and dividend accounts by transferring their balances to retained earnings
Only temporary accounts are closed; permanent accounts (assets, liabilities, equity) carry forward
The post-closing trial balance verifies that only permanent accounts remain with balances

faq.question: What is the difference between temporary and permanent accounts?
faq.answer: Temporary accounts (revenue, expenses, dividends) measure activity for a single period and are reset to zero during closing. Permanent accounts (assets, liabilities, equity) carry their balances forward from period to period and are never closed.

faq.question: What is a post-closing trial balance?
faq.answer: It's a listing of all accounts and their balances after closing entries have been posted. Only permanent accounts (balance sheet accounts) should appear. It verifies that debits still equal credits and that all temporary accounts have been properly closed to zero.
